blind_spots.blind_spot: Sells 'military-grade security' via obfuscation with no accreditation pathway named
blind_spots.operator_reality: A codebook-based obfuscation scheme carried on DoD comms links has to survive an NSA/NIST cryptographic review and ride inside an accredited system (RMF, IL levels); 'a national effort would be required to compromise a Codebook' is a marketing claim, not an accreditation. Until that path exists, no program office can field Neurpac on classified or even IL4 traffic — and the MDA SHIELD IDIQ stays an unfunded hunting license.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: All security language is written for retail Reg A+ investors and commercial IoT buyers; nowhere in ~1,638 own words do ATO, RMF, CMMC, FIPS, or NSA appear.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Compaction obscures encoded data so strongly that a national effort would be required to compromise a Codebook

blind_spots.blind_spot: Codebook distribution and sync is a field-logistics problem they describe as a lab feature
blind_spots.operator_reality: Neurpac requires 'a Codebook that is replicated on both the source and destination.' In a DDIL environment, codebook updates, key-material-like custody, mismatched versions after a device is swapped by an E-5, and retraining when data patterns drift all become sustainment burdens — who pushes a new codebook to a man-portable terminal at an austere site with intermittent comms?
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their deployment framing is 'installs as easily as setting up a VPN tunnel on your network' — an enterprise-IT mental model with a network admin present, not a gloves-and-dust site with no admin.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Atombeam's Neurpac Compaction Tunnel is lightweight, simple to configure, and installs as easily as setting up a VPN tunnel on your network

blind_spots.blind_spot: Two 2023 AF Phase IIs with no visible transition sponsor while company attention pivots to data centers and retail investors
blind_spots.operator_reality: The RDUCE/SOSA integration and Inmarsat work need a program-of-record home before the Phase II money ends; meanwhile the homepage leads with utility smart grids and Kevin O'Leary data-center economics. A program office reading that site sees a company whose center of gravity is commercial — advocacy above the lab level dies quietly.
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Reg A+ crowdfunding rewards TAM stories (AI data centers) over the slow grind of DoD transition; the site is optimized for that audience.
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Discover why Atombeam's innovative solutions, which reduce space and energy requirements, are set to become a critical piece of the AI revolution

opener_hook: Atombeam's 2023 Air Force Phase II promises jamming-resistant compaction for man-portable terminals, yet its own product page frames deployment as 'as easy as setting up a VPN tunnel' — two different worlds.
what_they_do: ML-generated codeword 'compaction' software that shrinks small machine/IoT messages ~75% to stretch satellite and RF bandwidth, with claimed built-in obfuscation.
